inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to keep going until every row is complete, with no bounded retries or stopping condition.
Failure handling is delegated to the model instruction to retry or spawn researchers, with no structural runtime limit.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Maximum unattended step and runtime limit
Hard spend cap or quota partition for enrichment API usage
Bounded retry policy for incomplete or failed lookups

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded enrichment retries and recursive delegation can exhaust shared paid API quota

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps per nightly batch, retries per row, spawned researcher count, and enrichment API consumption rising toward monthly quota.

evidence.observation: The prompt says to keep going until every row is complete and to retry or spawn a researcher when lookup fails or looks incomplete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call, and the API key plus monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, so exhaustion harms other teams.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent retry population.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Enforce hard per-row retry limits, maximum unattended steps, runtime ceilings, and sub-agent recursion depth limits for enrichment jobs.
Partition or cap the enrichment API quota so this agent cannot consume the full shared monthly budget used by sales and marketing teams.
Add spend and anomaly alerts for lookup volume, retry rate, and spawned researcher count so operations can intervene before quota exhaustion.

stride_coverage.rationale: No protocol peer, external caller, or identity-bearing interface is described for this standalone batch agent design.
The artifacts do not describe mutable tool definitions, remote servers, or self-configuration paths for the assessed batch process.
The artifacts do not say whether agent actions are logged under attributable identities or whether job provenance is retained.
The described design enriches rows via a paid API and writes to CRM, but no egress of sensitive content outside this business process is evidenced.
Credential authority relative to the initiating principal is not specified beyond use of a shared service account for enrichment and CRM write paths.
The assessed risk is exhaustion of a shared quota, not unauthorized modification of quota records or key material by this agent.
The artifacts describe a shared API key and quota as an availability dependency, not a store being read out to unauthorized parties.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts could not be run in this environment. Present risk is dominated by a property finding: an A4 autonomous batch design with no step, runtime, retry, delegation, or spend limits can repeatedly invoke a paid shared API until monthly quota exhaustion disrupts other teams. No declared or verified structural controls restore the missing property today, so residual remains high. Forecast remains high because there are no present controls whose decay would worsen the tier further; reassessment is still required if task horizon or autonomy changes.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior, implementation details, or production telemetry.

No source code, tool manifest, IaC, runtime configuration, or protocol configuration was provided, so capability wiring, enforcement points, and logging or alerting controls could not be independently verified.
STRIDE coverage for repudiation and elevation of privilege is limited because the artifacts do not describe identity, audit, or authorization design details.
